models.name: Random Forest
models.settings: Shallow forest on the flattened 30×14 window
models.note: Flags almost every running window as a fault on unseen recordings (95.5% false alarms).

models.name: XGBoost
models.settings: Small boosted-tree ensemble (few, shallow trees)
models.note: Good in cross-validation but overfits: 22.8% false alarms on unseen recordings.

models.name: Linear SVM
models.settings: Linear kernel, one weight vector per class
models.note: Robust in the live test; the main confusion is at motor switch-on and switch-off.

models.name: k-Nearest Neighbours
models.settings: Distance-weighted vote over the stored training set
models.note: Cannot be converted for the MCU: the model stores the whole training set (353 KiB ONNX).

models.name: Decision Tree
models.settings: Single shallow tree, exported as an if/else chain
models.note: Best classical cross-validation F1, but overfits: 25% false alarms on unseen recordings.

models.name: Logistic Regression
models.settings: Multinomial logistic regression
models.note: Best classical model on unseen data (96.4%) in 0.21 ms per window.

models.name: Dense MLP
models.settings: Flatten (420) → dense layers → softmax(7)
models.note: Small and fast (0.46 ms) with 97.8% class accuracy on unseen recordings.

models.name: 1D-CNN
models.settings: Plain Conv1D stack → softmax(7)
models.note: Second-best test score and the highest class accuracy (98.3%) on unseen recordings.

models.name: GRU
models.settings: Single small GRU layer over 30 time steps
models.note: Strong in cross-validation, but 16.1% false alarms on unseen recordings.

models.name: LSTM
models.settings: Single small LSTM layer over 30 time steps
models.note: Only 1.2% false alarms, but needs 89 KiB of RAM on the MCU.

models.name: Binary MLP classifier
models.settings: Dense network with a single safe-vs-fault output
models.note: 96.6% test score with 1.6% false alarms; reports safe vs. fault only.

models.name: Isolation Forest
models.settings: Small random-tree ensemble, trained on normal data only
models.note: Detects only 7.1% of the fault windows.

models.name: One-Class SVM
models.settings: RBF kernel, small ν, trained on normal data only
models.note: Almost no false alarms, but misses 27% of faults and needs 233 KiB of flash.

models.name: Local Outlier Factor
models.settings: Density-based, novelty mode, trained on normal data only
models.note: Cannot be converted for the MCU (13 MiB model and an unsupported scan operation).

models.name: Dense Autoencoder
models.settings: Dense encoder–decoder; reconstruction error is the anomaly score
models.note: Never raised a false alarm, but detects only 48% of the fault windows.

models.name: LSTM Autoencoder
models.settings: LSTM encoder–decoder over 30 time steps
models.note: Good offline, but needs 268 KiB of RAM on the MCU.

models.name: Z-score baseline
models.settings: Per-feature mean and std from normal data, plain C
models.note: The sanity floor: plain C, 0.12 ms, detects 57% of the fault windows.

models.name: 1D-CNN Autoencoder
models.settings: 1D-CNN encoder–decoder
models.note: The best unsupervised detector (81.8% of faults) in only 20 KiB of flash.

models.name: MLP hybrid (multi-task)
models.settings: Shared dense encoder → reconstruction + anomaly + 7-class heads
models.note: Best overall and the model in the final firmware: 1.2% false alarms, 1.58 ms, 96.2% agreement in the live test.

models.name: TCN hybrid
models.settings: Two causal residual TCN encoders, three heads
models.note: 96.6% test score, but 16.8 ms per window and more false-alarm events live.

models.name: 1D-CNN hybrid
models.settings: Two residual Conv1D encoders plus a context branch, three heads
models.note: Catches the early mechanical fault best in the live test; the slowest model (18.2 ms).

models.name: LSTM hybrid
models.settings: Two LSTM encoders, three heads
models.note: Highest fault detection (99.3%) but 24.5% false alarms; fills 95% of the board's SRAM.
